shortDescription: A German branch of the Iranian state-owned lender Bank Sepah has been declared insolvent in the wake of sanctions, Germany's financial regulator BaFin said on Thursday.($1 = 0.8592 euros)

children: A German branch of the Iranian state-owned lender Bank Sepah has been declared insolvent in the wake of sanctions, Germany's financial regulator BaFin said on Thursday.
The bank is one of Iran's largest public banks, ​with historical links to the military.
"The institution is no longer able to repay its customers' deposits," said the regulator.
The bank's Frankfurt location did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment.
"As a result of European Union sanctions against Bank Sepah, the German branch no longer has access to the European payments system," BaFin said.
BaFin said a Frankfurt court on Thursday appointed an insolvency manager.
BaFin stressed that the bank is not systemically relevant with total assets of €50 million ($58.20 million) and just 11 depositors, meaning there is no "threat to financial stability".
